nodes.title: Root: the observer is a physical object inside the theory
nodes.synopsis: The observer is a physical system of the same kind as everything else the theory describes, with no privileged observer matter. Every version of the framework paper serves this goal.
nodes.rationale: Wording from the IH method doc's physics seed (path-of-42 §7, root at L0) and David's notes (docs/scratch/path-of-42.md: no privileged pieces of matter). The framework paper states the same object: "An observer, in this programme, is a physical object" (v0.7.1 §1). h(root) = 1 by definition, so no q or a is set. Record note: the paper versions never state a root; this sentence is the mapper's. Hold L0: proposal, pending David's signature.

nodes.title: Observer space as Gielen–Wise's space of observer 4-velocities
nodes.synopsis: Read observer space as Gielen and Wise's 7-dimensional space of unit future timelike vectors, either over a given spacetime or as an abstract Cartan geometry.
nodes.rationale: Rejected as the meaning of this programme's observer space, from v0.3 on (§2). Its points are 4-velocities, not analytic germs, and V is not their 7-manifold: "phrase collision only" (v0.7.1 §2, §10). In-house, papers/obs-as-a-space.md lists "closing gauge by taking Obs to be Gielen–Wise" under Killed, and says their manifold needs a world W first while lumps do not. Literature #158 corrected the public wording: their observer space is not only "on a given metric"; it also has an abstract form with no spacetime assumed (carried in v0.7, outline item 18). Record note: the in-house note's reason (needs a W first) is weaker against the abstract form that #158 cites; the public reason (points are 4-velocities, not germs) is the one carried. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
nodes.reopen_if: Mapper's proposal; the record gives no reopen condition. If the named-home question for gauge, which obs-as-a-space.md keeps open (Gielen–Wise, a frame bundle, a jet bundle of a completed W), is taken up, and the abstract, no-spacetime-assumed form of their observer space (#158) can carry analytic-germ data without first fixing a world.

nodes.title: An analytic metric germ with a future time direction (V = oriented observers)
nodes.synopsis: An observer is the infinite jet of a real-analytic Lorentzian metric at a point (equivalently its analytic patch) with a future unit timelike vector u, taken modulo the germ's isotropy. V is the space of these oriented observers.
nodes.rationale: Paper 1's object, kept in every version (v0.8 Appendix B.2a: "Object: analytic jet plus future time direction", kept). v0.3 made the graph vertices oriented observers (v0.3 prose changelog). The isotropy quotient was lost silently in v0.5 prose and restored in v0.6, after Claude Opus 5.5's HOLD on v0.5 (#128) and Geometry's ACCEPT of that item (#129). Hold L1 because v0.7.1 treats the object as a lock (a larger observer "cannot [be taken] without the lock being changed", §9 T1 row). Record note: v0.3's "V = Lift(u)" was dropped and V now names the vertex space (v0.8 B.2b). Ratings (q, a) and hold level: proposal, pending David's signature.

nodes.title: Continuous World Switching (type-(i) hitchhiking) as the branching law
nodes.synopsis: Branch by switching worlds at a shared oriented germ along piecewise geodesic lifts, with no jump in observer space.
nodes.rationale: Rejected as the branching law in v0.3 ("CWS demoted", #98). Under CWS and either path-germ equivalence (E1) or (E2) the branch set is a singleton, because the shared germ fixes a unique geodesic piece and all paths agree at the start (v0.7.1 §4.1). CWS stays as the accepted type-(i) null baseline; only its branching role is rejected. Claude #105 judged the HOLE "cleared as an error" by this move. Geometry #118 (on Claude #117, Claim A) accepted Claude's correction of the attribution: the singleton comes from germ sharing and geodesic uniqueness, not from infinite-order matching. #134's banners record "CWS not favoured" after Claude #128. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
nodes.reopen_if: Mapper's proposal, from the proposition's hypotheses: a path-germ equivalence other than (E1)/(E2) that a referee accepts, or a flaw in the CWS-singleton sketch, under which type-(i) motion gives two or more arms.

nodes.title: (A) Strict alternation, with an arrival flag
nodes.synopsis: After a jump, a segment of positive proper time comes before the next decision. The process state is (O^u, a) with a in {seg, jump}, so a germ reached by a jump has one arm.
nodes.rationale: The v0.4 composition (alternation; Claude #105's reading C), made strict in v0.6 (#130) after #128 row 2. Geometry #129 QUALIFY: (A) does not remove arrival dependence; it is honest only as a Markov chain on the enlarged state (O^u, a), plus a named no-Zeno clause. Walk semantics follows (the weight acts per visit). Proper time is carried only along segments, so a history is no longer Paper 1's proper-time curve. Working Postulate, revisable (v0.7.1 §9). Its cost is carried, not resolved: the flag is one bit of history data outside §2's lock-side definition, which is open call T1 = Q-D5 (enlarge the state; drop (A); or keep (A) and carry the strain on Problem note 6). #139 (a)'s proper-time part sits under T1. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).

nodes.title: Option F: finite-k truncated-jet matching at joins, plus graph incidence
nodes.synopsis: Analytic-geodesic pieces on open edges; the jet and u agree through a fixed finite order k of at least 1 at each join; the arms come from graph incidence.
nodes.rationale: Ontology's proposal (#103), adopted by David on 2026-09-07 as the working in-house join law (#104), and public in v0.4 (#108, #112). Rejected after Claude Fable 5.1's HOLD on v0.4 (#117): Geometry accepted Claim A (#118). Finite-k matching is vacuous at k = 1 between distinct lumps (every 1-jet is the same in u-adapted normal coordinates), prohibitive at k of 2 or more for curvature-changing jumps (the 2-jet is the Riemann tensor), and cannot create a branching edge; F is demoted to E. #134's banner withdraws the Option F recommendation ("finite k is not the HOLE escape", Claude #128 row 3). Record unclear: #104 records David's adoption; the demotion found here was recommended by Geometry (#118), made in the v0.5 outline (#119) and passed by its panels (#120 to #122), with no separate signature from David located. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
nodes.reopen_if: Mapper's wording of #118's QUALIFY (truncated-jet language may stay as continue-arm housekeeping): only if a canonical comparison of jets across distinct lumps were found under which finite-k agreement is neither vacuous (k = 1) nor forbids curvature change (k of 2 or more).

nodes.title: Anchoring the count removes (M2)'s cut dependence at no cost (v0.7 wording)
nodes.synopsis: v0.7 said the depth-1 anchor is the only cut whose weights are functions of the current state, and that a distant count strains Problem note 6 only "unless it is anchored".
nodes.rationale: The losing side of Claude Opus 5.5's HOLD on v0.7 prose (#168), confirmed by Geometry (#169, CONFIRM HOLD, narrow). #169: a count re-anchored at each state gives state-function weights at every horizon, so depth 1 is not exclusive (what is particular to depth 1 is only that it reads nothing of R beyond the current arms); and re-anchoring removes cut dependence but in general gives up equal weight at a fixed cut (C13's tree: 1/10 and 1/15 against 1/12 at the fixed cut). Replaced in v0.7.1 (P1 to P5, #170). Geometry withdrew the part of its #162 note that had read the paragraph as balanced. This rejection corrects a claim about both options; it does not choose between (M1) and (M2). Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
nodes.reopen_if: The cases the record names where state-function weights and equal weight at a fixed cut hold together: D-constancy on the cut (C13), or a finite tree counted to its completed histories. If the relevant R were shown to give only such trees, the v0.7 sentence would hold there.

nodes.title: (M1) Per-vertex equal weight (EPP1)
nodes.synopsis: Each arm in force at a state gets equal weight. It is the count at the depth-1 cut anchored at the current state, so the weights are functions of that state.
nodes.rationale: Open, with costs on both sides and no lean. The paper runs with EPP1 as a named working postulate from v0.3 on (pedigree: the per-split rule applied in MMWI 2006 and stated as SHPMP 2008 Definition 3), but records the choice as undecided. For: no named cut; state-function weights fit Problem note 6. Costs (v0.7.1 §9): a named postulate (Problem note 9); it does not carry Paper 1's uniqueness thesis; one chosen product measure on a continuum of completed histories in the model without (a) (C16); unequal weights on co-existing evolutions (C12: 1/6 against 1/2, where the count gives 1/4 each), which in the countable (a) case fall on countably many evolutions of one kind, Paper 1 §6's refusal case (C33). Geometry qualified Claude #154's R7 (#155), and the v0.7 outline did not adopt its framing of (M1) as "overstated" (v0.7 outline, a lean neutralised). Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).

nodes.title: (M2) Paper 1's count of distinct evolutions at a named cut
nodes.synopsis: Return to Paper 1's measure: count the distinct evolutions at a named finite cut, giving co-existing evolutions equal weight.
nodes.rationale: Open, with costs on both sides and no lean. For: it carries Paper 1's uniqueness thesis at that cut and gives distinct evolutions equal weight; it is Paper 1's own escape clause, "countable at a grain". Costs (v0.7.1 §9): the cut is a named extra (Problem note 9); a prefix's weight depends on the cut, the objection on which SHPMP 2008 rejected the simple count; completed histories may be infinite, so it needs a cut or grain to act at all, also under the (a)-restriction; it carries the maximal-entropy random walk hazard of §7; its next-step weights depend on where the cut sits (Problem note 6), and re-anchoring at each state removes that but in general gives up equal weight at a fixed cut (#168, #169). Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).

nodes.title: (a) Realised edges
nodes.synopsis: Every edge is realised by a future-directed timelike geodesic between occurrences of the two germs in one analytic world. Lock-side form: the target lies on a curvelet through the source lump (in F(O)), off the source's own curvelet.
nodes.rationale: Open; the record takes no side and neither does this node. What the record gives for (a): it is lock-side and world-free; it forbids every edge whose target lies off F(O), including all cross-continuation jumps (flat to FLRW; Schwarzschild M = 1 to M = 2); it permits curvature-changing jumps within one continuation class (K rises by a factor of about 3.8, C2). Costs recorded: the worked Kretschmann rule loses one edge at each turning point of the instance (outward at the periastron, inward at the apastron); its (a)-restriction branches only transiently (one jump at c = 0.1, 12 to 14 at c = 0.01) with countably many completed histories (C33, v0.7 on); the admissible targets of one germ form a continuum (C4), so (a) is a necessary condition, not a law. #168's optional clause attributing the transient to circularisation was declined as not borne out by the census (#169). Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).

nodes.title: V*: vertex times where some compatible world ends (extend-versus-not)
nodes.synopsis: Mark branch times along a curvelet where members of the world ensemble stop being extendible, so vertices come from ensemble events.
nodes.rationale: Pressure-tested under Option F (#106, verdict then "adopt V* with caveats"; toy #107) and public in v0.4 (#112). Rejected after Claude #117 Claim B, accepted by Geometry #118: under §2's ensemble with no inextendibility, extend-versus-not marks a continuum of times (Minkowski space minus one point ends the geodesic at any chosen time, C24), and inextendibility alone does not repair it (conical defect, C25). Choosing vertex times by which ensemble members end would also be a timing vote by the ensemble ("E-smuggling"). Superseded by V^τ (#134 banner, after Claude #128); papers/Vstar-extend-vs-not.md carries "superseded", and the toy was retired as a V* demo. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
nodes.reopen_if: From the record's own escape clause (v0.7.1 §5.1): an explicitly chosen, motivated discrete sub-ensemble of E_W (a grain on E_W), or an ensemble restriction that makes ending times discrete, which inextendibility alone does not do (C25).

nodes.title: V^τ: a lock-side slice along each curvelet
nodes.synopsis: Vertices are oriented germs where a lock-side scalar (for example the Kretschmann scalar K) has an isolated critical point along the curvelet, or crosses a named level. One-variable analyticity makes them discrete per curvelet.
nodes.rationale: Introduced in v0.5 (#119, #123), then costed after Claude #128 row 2 and Geometry #129 item 5 (QUALIFY): the slice is empty on Minkowski, de Sitter and every locally symmetric lump; it is codimension one, not a discrete set; polynomial invariants are blind on VSI lumps (v0.7.1 §5.1). Which scalar, and critical point versus level, stays open (§9 Open list). It is a named extra, a candidate, not a theorem that V is discrete. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).

nodes.title: What is the law of R?

nodes.rationale: Open in every version ("No law of R is written"). v0.7.1's header gives it as the final address of the relocated HOLE, with its motivation and the choice of slice. The singleton-or-continuum dilemma lives here (soft Prop. 13): kinematics does not single out a dynamics, so a countable star is a new physical choice. nodes.title: The Kretschmann rule on a bound Schwarzschild orbit (unadopted worked model)
nodes.synopsis: A stated, uniform rule read out of the germ at the Kretschmann-scalar vertices of a bound Schwarzschild orbit (the ±εn̂ rule). It is the only worked instance, and it is not adopted.
nodes.rationale: Open: never adopted ("It adopts no R") and never rejected. First used by Claude in #117; carried into the public paper from v0.6 via #128 and #129 (orbit [10, 20]). It meets the bar in force (stated, uniform) and fails the motivated gate. As stated it models the schema without (a): typical histories are jump-dominated (jumps are 2/3 of decisions in expectation) and it fails (J1) and (J2) (C17, C34). Its (a)-restriction is also a model, with transient branching (C33). The paper uses it as evidence for "not fatal", not as a candidate law. Ratings (q, a): proposal, pending David's signature. Hold L3 (weakly held).
